name: GA-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by 15 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Austin Scott holds a massive fundraising edge ($1.1M raised, $1.3M on hand vs. under $20K for the Democrat)
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 95%
No general-election polling or expert ratings available, leaving fundamentals as the main guide
model.rationale: This rural Georgia seat is structurally Republican, and Austin Scott pairs incumbency with an overwhelming financial advantage over a barely funded challenger. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican win, with only modest uncertainty from the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the challenger within single digits, or a surge of outside spending on the Democratic side, would be the first sign this race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Georgia's 8th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 15 points toward the GOP. Austin Scott has held the seat since 2011 and is running again with the advantages of incumbency and a well-stocked campaign account. He has raised roughly $1.1 million and holds $1.3 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Kelly Esti has raised under $20,000 and reports minimal cash, with no outside spending on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert race ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price the Republican near 95 percent. The expected margin is a comfortable Republican win in the mid-to-high teens, with a small but nonzero chance of an upset given the lack of direct polling.
